title: Inventory engine capability requirements and enforce bead ownership
description:
Owns the PACK-TO-ENGINE boundary: what capabilities the clause corpus requires,
who owns each one, and proof that nothing is invisible. It does NOT implement
them — engine implementation lives in the separate top-level epic eshyra-olc5
("Reopen deterministic engine completeness under the clause-capability
contract"), where engine:F1..engine:F10 now hang.

Why the split: the PACK question is whether the data completely and accurately
expresses the rules; the ENGINE question is whether Eshyra can execute what the
pack expresses. Those must interact but must never again collapse into one
undifferentiated "modeled" status. An engine-pending clause is not automatically
a pack defect.

Two beads, two lifecycle stages:
  19.5.1  BOOTSTRAP ledger — startable immediately, from artifacts/code/beads/
          findings/known-missing clauses. Not derivable from the pack alone.
  19.5.12 AUTHORITATIVE ledger — regenerated from the clause-complete corpus
          after 19.1.1, 19.1.4 and 19.6.1, then diffed against the bootstrap.

*** TAXONOMY WARNING — READ BEFORE TOUCHING ANY CAPABILITY BEAD ***
"F1".."F10" means three different things in this project:
 (1) engine:F1..F10 — values of data.executionReadiness.clauses[].engineHooks[]
     .engine in the committed pack. THIS is what the capability beads mean.
     Verified at 4384f25 (hook references): F1 83, F2 226, F3 31, F4 169,
     F5 399, F6 46, F7 15, F8 310, F9 236, F10 9.
 (2) eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10 — a CLOSED epic with a DIFFERENT taxonomy: F1
     dice-grammar, F2 action-economy budget, F3 concentration/active-effects,
     F4 spell-slot economy, F5 usage/recharge/attunement, F6 death/dying/HP-
     buffer, F7 rest engine, F8 character-build gap closures, F9 derived-math
     primitives, F10 currency surface. Only F2/F3/F5/F7 roughly correspond.
     NEVER assume a same-numbered eshyra-2n1t child covers an engine:F family.
 (3) fable:F1..F8 — Fable 5 audit findings (e.g. fable:F1 = unsupported Starting
     Wealth table). Unrelated to both; owned by the B/C/D beads.

CANONICAL ALIAS PREFIXES — use these everywhere; never a bare "F1" or "CAP-001":
  engine:F1 .. engine:F10     pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1 .. fable:F8        Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01 .. opus:F-35      Opus 5 original + amended audit findings
  sol:CAP-001 .. sol:CAP-014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001 .. indep:012      independent review (formerly "SOL-001..012"; renamed
                              so it stops colliding with the sol: model-name prefix)
acceptance_criteria:
- Every engine-pending, partial, unimplemented and design-blocked clause maps to a real open bead in eshyra-olc5 or an approved explicit house-rule/design dependency.
- No engine gap is excused because the pack is data-complete.
- The three deliberate SRD source ambiguities remain under eshyra-jhpt.6/.7 and are regression-tested as unresolved, never "fixed".
- Every capability requirement is expressed as a generated membership query, not a hand-copied count.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
